Subject: Severe latency + 502s right now (region us-west)

- If true, this explains both increased p99 and elevated 5xx rates due to request timeouts.

Ben/Evelyn — please confirm whether this is a config regression (recent autoscaler/prefetch change) or an emergent workload pattern. Laura/Marissa, I’ll flag for Exec if this needs leadership attention.

Summary of what I’ve pulled so far (initial triage):
- Telemetry: A sustained increase in prefetch retries starting 07:48; prefetch queue depth increased 7x for several hot prefixes.
- KV subsystem: noticeable cache churn on several popular prefixes. Miss rate spiked from 2% -> 18% for the window.
- Batching: the batcher observed lane starvation on some GPUs — long blocking windows (~600ms) where a single hot key overheard lanes and prevented flush.

Immediate mitigations I’ve applied:
1) Temporarily lowered max-prefetch-concurrency on the affected pool to reduce simultaneous reloads (rolled at 08:55).
2) Short-circuited a small proportion of requests to a conservative model variant that bypasses prefetch for reads (routing rule).

Early results: 502s decreased but p99 still elevated (~800–1,200ms). I’ve attached a snapshot of the kv_config (kv_config_snapshot.json) and the trace that Alicia provided — see annotated notes in perf_trace.log inside the zip.

Next steps: Evelyn to validate whether a config rollback (last change 02-28) is warranted, and Laura/Marissa to decide if this warrants an immediate executive notification (customers affected: Acme AI + Faraday internal load).

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: kv_config_snapshot.json

Subject: Re: Severe latency + 502s right now (region us-west)

Ben — good work. I’ve dug into the 02-28 rollout logs: we did increase the aggressive_prefetch_threshold and enabled wider prefetch fanout for the us-west pool to improve throughput for a specific high-volume customer test. That config change likely amplified simultaneous reloads for a small set of hot prefixes.

Hypothesis: the prefetch fanout + higher concurrency created a positive feedback loop: many requests tried to prefetch the same KV prefix, cache thrash occurred, and queueing/backpressure led to long wait windows (observed batcher starvation).

Recommended actions (short term):
- Roll back the 02-28 prefetch fanout/concurrency changes for the us-west pool (I can roll back now).
- Introduce a short-lived per-prefix prefetch lock (coalesce reloads) — apply as a patch with a kill-switch.
- Customer-facing: reduce max-concurrency for affected routes and enable the conservative model variant as default while we stabilize.

I’ll prepare a one-pager for Exec describing root cause and mitigations. If Exec wants to get involved, loop in Marissa/Markus.

Evelyn
Lead, Runtime Engineering
